visual_design_observations: Monumental, near-symmetrical Beaux-Arts / Neoclassical composition; the central portico must read differently from the long side wings.
Pale white-to-warm-stone plaster; restrained weathering and subtle tonal variation rather than a single flat white material.
Four giant Corinthian columns in the central projecting bay; capitals, shafts, bases and column shadows need separate geometry.
Deep entablature, layered cornices and a triangular sculpted pediment; relief silhouette should be modeled as a raised feature, not a flat dark decal.
Tall rectangular multi-pane windows with dark frames, repeated by floor and aligned in vertical bays; pilasters and shallow window surrounds between bays.
Central balconies/corbels and stepped entrance platform; multiple door openings and clear depth at the portico.
Long side wings, corner column groups, roofline cornice and repeated window rhythm; avoid a simple rectangular prism.
Building is documented as four stories with a rectangular plan and internal courtyards; the footprint must preserve courtyard voids if present in the authoritative geometry.
modeling_plan: Verify the footprint polygon and orientation against official coordinates and repository photos; split museum complex polygons into individual structures if needed.
Build a four-storey base mass with floor-band offsets and shallow pilasters, then a separately modeled projecting central portico.
Create repeated windows as grouped modules; model frames, recesses, sills and lintels with varied depth.
Create column shafts, bases and stylized Corinthian capitals as distinct meshes; add a layered entablature and pediment relief.
Add entrance steps, plinth, balconies/corbels, cornices, parapet/roofline, and subtle material/weathering variation.
Keep sculptural detail procedural and clearly labeled as a visual approximation unless directly traced from a licensed close-up.
do_not_do: Do not assign the facade to a generic nearby polygon.
Do not treat the National Museum complex as one building without confirming its separate footprints.
Do not claim photogrammetric or surveyed accuracy.

targets.name: Cancer Institute Building, Philippine General Hospital

location.coordinates_status: exact footprint coordinate not yet verified

repository_references.match: Photo description identifies the Cancer Institute facade on Padre Faura Street

visual_design_observations: Historic institutional facade with a projecting central portico and a triangular/classical pediment.
Pale lavender-grey/off-white plaster with visible age and uneven weathering; use subtle mottling and paint variation, not dramatic damage.
Four tall rectangular columns at the central entrance; deep shadows behind the portico make the central bay read as recessed.
Wide entablature and cornice with small repeated ornamental blocks; pediment and fascia should be layered.
Tall vertical openings and multi-pane windows on the wings; keep their rhythm distinct from the entrance portico.
Roof edge has a muted reddish tone in the reference; model the roof/cap as a separate material surface.
The photo contains temporary canopies, tables, chairs, a vehicle and people; exclude these from the permanent building model unless separately treated as removable scene props.
Facade lettering in the reference is historical signage; only reproduce readable text when the text is legible and the orientation/placement is verified.
modeling_plan: Identify the exact Cancer Institute footprint among PGH campus buildings before applying any facade details.
Create the institutional massing, raised central portico, four columns, deep entablature, pediment and cornice as separate meshes.
Model window recesses, frames and repeated openings on each wing; avoid applying generic balconies or a generic storefront door.
Use aged pale lavender-grey plaster with mild variation and darker recesses; keep the roof edge muted red.
Add the historic sign as a separate, editable mesh/texture asset only after confirming exact wording and scale.
Keep temporary waiting-area objects out of the base building GLB so the building remains reusable.
do_not_do: Do not attach this facade to PGH Central Block, OPD or another named building without evidence.
Do not bake the tents, chairs, car or people into the building geometry.
Do not infer exact floor heights or dimensions from one perspective photo.
